title: Microsoft 365 Backup: longer recovery windows for SharePoint and OneDrive, up to 10 years
summary: Hold: the guidance incorrectly says backup history before the date a window was lengthened does not exist. Microsoft says available history depends on when protection began and which recovery points have not expired, not simply when the window was changed.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: History before the date a recovery window was lengthened does not exist, and history beyond one year is available only for periods after protection began under the longer window.
claims.quote: Restore points start being generated when you create the backup policy ... Only recovery points that have been generated and haven't expired are available.
claims.fix: Replace the At rollout bullet with 'Record the date each window was lengthened; increasing it does not create older recovery points or recover expired ones.' Replace 'Tell restore owners that history beyond one year only exists for periods after protection began under the longer window' with 'Tell restore owners that available history depends on when protection began and which recovery points have not expired.' These statements are documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/backup/backup-whats-new and https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/backup/backup-restore-data?view=o365-worldwide#considerations-when-using-restore; add the latter to sources.

claims.where: front matter: risk; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The medium risk rating is justified by opt-in extensions and the effects of administrators subsequently reducing a window.
claims.quote: risk: "medium"; rationale: 'The change is opt-in per policy'; Why it matters: 'the one-year default stays until an administrator edits a policy'. The scale defines low as 'nothing happens until an admin opts in'.
claims.fix: Set risk to 'low' and replace the risk rationale with 'Low. Existing policies keep their one-year recovery window unless an administrator changes them. Longer windows retain deleted content for longer, and a later reduction deletes older recovery points after a 30-day grace period.'

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout

claims.quote: 'Check which roles can edit policies ... and remove the role from anyone who should not be able to shorten a window.' The table contains only recovery-window configuration and backup activity logs.
claims.fix: The Before rollout role-assignment review/removal step has no controls-table row. Remove that checklist bullet; keep the documented role information in Scope and Governance controls. Do not add a new control row as part of this correction.
